500   * %IDN2_TRANSITIONAL to enable Unicode TR46 transitional processing,
   501   * and %IDN2_NONTRANSITIONAL to enable Unicode TR46 non-transitional
   502   * processing.  Multiple flags may be specified by binary or:ing them
   503   * together, for example %IDN2_ALABEL_ROUNDTRIP |
   504   * %IDN2_NONTRANSITIONAL.  The %IDN2_NFC_INPUT in @flags is always
   505   * enabled in this function.
   506   *
   507   * After version 0.11: @lookupname may be NULL to test lookup of @src
   508   * without allocating memory.
   509   *
   510   * Returns: On successful conversion %IDN2_OK is returned, if
   511   *   conversion from locale to UTF-8 fails then %IDN2_ICONV_FAIL is
   512   *   returned, if the output domain or any label would have been too
   513   *   long %IDN2_TOO_BIG_DOMAIN or %IDN2_TOO_BIG_LABEL is returned, or
   514   *   another error code is returned.
   515   *
   516   * Since: 0.1
   517   **/
   518  int
   519  idn2_lookup_ul (const char * src, char ** lookupname, int flags)
   520  {
   521    uint8_t *utf8src = NULL;
   522    int rc;
   523
   524    if (src)
   525      {
   526        const char *encoding = locale_charset ();
   527
   528        utf8src = u8_strconv_from_encoding (src, encoding, iconveh_error);
   529
   530        if (!utf8src)
   531          {
   532            if (errno == ENOMEM)
   533              return IDN2_MALLOC;
   534            return IDN2_ICONV_FAIL;
   535          }
   536      }
   537
   538    rc = idn2_lookup_u8 (utf8src, (uint8_t **) lookupname,
   539                         flags | IDN2_NFC_INPUT);
   540
   541    free (utf8src);
   542
   543    return rc;
   544  }

   546  /**
   547   * idn2_to_ascii_4i:
   548   * @input: zero terminated input Unicode (UCS-4) string.
   549   * @inlen: number of elements in @input.
   550   * @output: pointer to newly allocated zero-terminated output string.
   551   * @flags: optional #idn2_flags to modify behaviour.
   552   *
   553   * The ToASCII operation takes a sequence of Unicode code points that make
   554   * up one domain label and transforms it into a sequence of code points in
   555   * the ASCII range (0..7F). If ToASCII succeeds, the original sequence and
   556   * the resulting sequence are equivalent labels.
   557   *
   558   * It is important to note that the ToASCII operation can fail.
   559   * ToASCII fails if any step of it fails. If any step of the
   560   * ToASCII operation fails on any label in a domain name, that domain
   561   * name MUST NOT be used as an internationalized domain name.
   562   * The method for dealing with this failure is application-specific.
   563   *
   564   * The inputs to ToASCII are a sequence of code points.
   565   *
   566   * ToASCII never alters a sequence of code points that are all in the ASCII
   567   * range to begin with (although it could fail). Applying the ToASCII operation multiple
   568   * effect as applying it just once.
   569   *
   570   * The default behavior of this function (when flags are zero) is to apply
   571   * the IDNA2008 rules without the TR46 amendments. As the TR46
   572   * non-transitional processing is nowadays ubiquitous, when unsure, it is
   573   * recommended to call this function with the %IDN2_NONTRANSITIONAL
   574   * and the %IDN2_NFC_INPUT flags for compatibility with other software.
   575   *
   576   * Return value: Returns %IDN2_OK on success, or error code.
   577   *
   578   * Since: 2.0.0
   579   **/
   580  int
   581  idn2_to_ascii_4i (const uint32_t * input, size_t inlen, char * output, int flags)
   582  {
   583    uint32_t *input_u32;
   584    uint8_t *input_u8, *output_u8;
   585    size_t length;
   586    int rc;
   587
   588    if (!input)
   589      {
   590        if (output)
   591          *output = 0;
   592        return IDN2_OK;
   593      }
   594
   595    input_u32 = (uint32_t *) malloc ((inlen + 1) * sizeof(uint32_t));
   596    if (!input_u32)
   597      return IDN2_MALLOC;
   598
   599    u32_cpy (input_u32, input, inlen);
   600    input_u32[inlen] = 0;
   601
   602    input_u8 = u32_to_u8 (input_u32, inlen + 1, NULL, &length);
   603    free (input_u32);
   604    if (!input_u8)
   605      {
   606        if (errno == ENOMEM)
   607          return IDN2_MALLOC;
   608        return IDN2_ENCODING_ERROR;
   609      }
   610
   611    rc = idn2_lookup_u8 (input_u8, &output_u8, flags);
   612    free (input_u8);
   613
   614    if (rc == IDN2_OK)
   615      {
   616        /* wow, this is ugly, but libidn manpage states:
   617         * char * out  output zero terminated string that must have room for at
   618         * least 63 characters plus the terminating zero.
   619         */
   620        if (output)
   621          strcpy (output, (const char *) output_u8);
   622
   623        free(output_u8);
   624      }
   625
   626    return rc;
   627  }

    43  int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *data, size_t size)
    44  {
    45          char *domain;
    46          char *out;
    47
    48          if (size > 1024)
    49                  return 0;
    50
    51          domain = (char *) malloc(size + 1);
    52          assert(domain != NULL);
    53
    54          /* 0 terminate */
    55          memcpy(domain, data, size);
    56          domain[size] = 0;
    57
    58          for (unsigned it = 0; it < sizeof(flags)/sizeof(flags[0]); it++) {
    59                  if (idn2_to_ascii_8z(domain, &out, flags[it]) == IDNA_SUCCESS)
    60                          idn2_free(out);
    61                  if (idn2_to_ascii_lz(domain, &out, flags[it]) == IDNA_SUCCESS)
    62                          idn2_free(out);
    63          }
    64
    65          if ((size & 3) == 0) {
    66                  uint32_t *u32 = (uint32_t *) malloc(size + 4);
    67                  char *out2 = (char *) malloc(64);
    68
    69                  assert(u32 != NULL);
    70                  assert(out2 != NULL);
    71
    72                  for (unsigned it = 0; it < sizeof(flags)/sizeof(flags[0]); it++)
    73                          idn2_to_ascii_4i((uint32_t *) data, size / 4, out2, flags[it]);
    74
    75                  memcpy(u32, data, size);
    76                  u32[size / 4] = 0;
    77
    78                  for (unsigned it = 0; it < sizeof(flags)/sizeof(flags[0]); it++)
    79                          if (idn2_to_ascii_4z(u32, &out, flags[it]) == IDN2_OK)
    80                            idn2_free(out);
    81
    82                  free(out2);
    83                  free(u32);
    84          }
    85
    86          free(domain);
    87          return 0;
    88  }

    66  /* Re-definitions to avoid modifying code below too much. */
    67  #define punycode_uint uint32_t
    68  #define punycode_success IDN2_OK
    69  #define punycode_overflow IDN2_PUNYCODE_OVERFLOW
    70  #define punycode_big_output IDN2_PUNYCODE_BIG_OUTPUT
    71  #define punycode_encode _idn2_punycode_encode

    73  /**********************************************************/
    74  /* Implementation (would normally go in its own .c file): */

    80  /*** Bootstring parameters for Punycode ***/
    81
    82  enum { base = 36, tmin = 1, tmax = 26, skew = 38, damp = 700,
    83         initial_bias = 72, initial_n = 0x80, delimiter = 0x2D };
    84
    85  /* basic(cp) tests whether cp is a basic code point: */
    86  #define basic(cp) ((punycode_uint)(cp) < 0x80)
    87
    88  /* encode_digit(d,flag) returns the basic code point whose value      */
    89  /* (when used for representing integers) is d, which needs to be in   */
    90  /* the range 0 to base-1.  The lowercase form is used unless flag is  */
    91  /* nonzero, in which case the uppercase form is used.  The behavior   */
    92  /* is undefined if flag is nonzero and digit d has no uppercase form. */
    93
    94  static char encode_digit(punycode_uint d, int flag)
    95  {
    96    return d + 22 + 75 * (d < 26) - ((flag != 0) << 5);
    97    /*  0..25 map to ASCII a..z or A..Z */
    98    /* 26..35 map to ASCII 0..9         */
    99  }

   101  /*** Platform-specific constants ***/
   102
   103  /* maxint is the maximum value of a punycode_uint variable: */
   104  static const punycode_uint maxint = -1;
   105  /* Because maxint is unsigned, -1 becomes the maximum value. */
   106
   107  /*** Bias adaptation function ***/
   108
   109  static punycode_uint adapt(
   110    punycode_uint delta, punycode_uint numpoints, int firsttime ) _GL_ATTRIBUTE_CONST;
   111
   112  static punycode_uint adapt(
   113    punycode_uint delta, punycode_uint numpoints, int firsttime )
   114  {
   115    punycode_uint k;
   116
   117    delta = firsttime ? delta / damp : delta >> 1;
   118    /* delta >> 1 is a faster way of doing delta / 2 */
   119    delta += delta / numpoints;
   120
   121    for (k = 0;  delta > ((base - tmin) * tmax) / 2;  k += base) {
   122      delta /= base - tmin;
   123    }
   124
   125    return k + (base - tmin + 1) * delta / (delta + skew);
   126  }

   128  /*** Main encode function ***/
   129
   130  int punycode_encode(
   131    size_t input_length_orig,
   132    const punycode_uint input[],
   133    size_t *output_length,
   134    char output[] )
   135  {
   136    punycode_uint input_length, n, delta, h, b, bias, j, m, q, k, t;
   137    size_t out, max_out;
   138
   139    /* The Punycode spec assumes that the input length is the same type */
   140    /* of integer as a code point, so we need to convert the size_t to  */
   141    /* a punycode_uint, which could overflow.                           */
   142
   143    if (input_length_orig > maxint) return punycode_overflow;
   144    input_length = (punycode_uint) input_length_orig;
   145
   146    /* Initialize the state: */
   147
   148    n = initial_n;
   149    delta = 0;
   150    out = 0;
   151    max_out = *output_length;
   152    bias = initial_bias;
   153
   154    /* Handle the basic code points: */
   155
   156    for (j = 0;  j < input_length;  ++j) {
   157      if (basic(input[j])) {
   158        if (max_out - out < 2) return punycode_big_output;
   159        output[out++] = (char) input[j];
   160      }
   161      /* else if (input[j] < n) return punycode_bad_input; */
   162      /* (not needed for Punycode with unsigned code points) */
   163    }
   164
   165    h = b = (punycode_uint) out;
   166    /* cannot overflow because out <= input_length <= maxint */
   167
   168    /* h is the number of code points that have been handled, b is the  */
   169    /* number of basic code points, and out is the number of ASCII code */
   170    /* points that have been output.                                    */
   171
   172    if (b > 0) output[out++] = delimiter;
   173
   174    /* Main encoding loop: */
   175
   176    while (h < input_length) {
   177      /* All non-basic code points < n have been     */
   178      /* handled already.  Find the next larger one: */
   179
   180      for (m = maxint, j = 0;  j < input_length;  ++j) {
   181        /* if (basic(input[j])) continue; */
   182        /* (not needed for Punycode) */
   183        if (input[j] >= n && input[j] < m) m = input[j];
   184      }
   185
   186      /* Increase delta enough to advance the decoder's    */
   187      /* <n,i> state to <m,0>, but guard against overflow: */
   188
   189      if (m - n > (maxint - delta) / (h + 1)) return punycode_overflow;
   190      delta += (m - n) * (h + 1);
   191      n = m;
   192
   193      for (j = 0;  j < input_length;  ++j) {
   194        /* Punycode does not need to check whether input[j] is basic: */
   195        if (input[j] < n /* || basic(input[j]) */ ) {
   196          if (++delta == 0) return punycode_overflow;
   197        }
   198
   199        if (input[j] == n) {
   200          /* Represent delta as a generalized variable-length integer: */
   201
   202          for (q = delta, k = base;  ;  k += base) {
   203            if (out >= max_out) return punycode_big_output;
   204            t = k <= bias /* + tmin */ ? tmin :     /* +tmin not needed */
   205                k >= bias + tmax ? tmax : k - bias;
   206            if (q < t) break;
   207            output[out++] = encode_digit(t + (q - t) % (base - t), 0);
   208            q = (q - t) / (base - t);
   209          }
   210
   211          output[out++] = encode_digit(q, 0);
   212          bias = adapt(delta, h + 1, h == b);
   213          delta = 0;
   214          ++h;
   215        }
   216      }
   217
   218      ++delta, ++n;
   219    }
   220
   221    *output_length = out;
   222    return punycode_success;
   223  }
